resumen: Seated facing a low pulley with the feet braced, you pull a handle towards your abdomen by driving the elbows back. A row with a still torso, without having to hold it bent over.
ejecucion: Sit facing the low pulley with your feet braced and knees slightly bent, and take the handle with your arms straight.
With your back straight and chest up, pull the handle towards your abdomen, driving your elbows back and close to your body.
At the end, squeeze your shoulder blades together without leaning back.
Return by straightening your arms under control, letting your shoulders come forward a little without rounding your back.
matices: The study comparing several lat exercises found one of the best lat-to-biceps ratios in the seated row, and the highest middle trapezius and rhomboid activity. Deliberately squeezing the shoulder blades did not change that activity. Differences between exercises were small.

fuentes.titulo: Variations in muscle activation levels during traditional latissimus dorsi weight training exercises: An experimental study
Comparison of different rowing exercises: trunk muscle activation and lumbar spine motion, load, and stiffness
fuentes.autor: Fenwick, Brown and McGill, J Strength Cond Res, 2009
